messages:
marie: Heads up — getting multiple p95/p99 alerts for text-gen endpoints since ~09:00 UTC. Support ticket #8673 opened with a couple of customer repros. Seems correlated with KV prefix miss rate spike.
aj: Thanks, linking ticket + grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/txgen/kvcache?orgId=1&from=now-1h. Miss rate jumped ~25% -> 45% on pool gpu-pool-east.
support-bot: Ticket #8673: customer 'AcmeHealth' reported+attached logs. Severity set to P2.
taylor: I can repro locally. Sequence length ~1024, and keys include per-request auth header fragments. Observed churn on node gpu-12: evictions per sec jumped. Repro steps:
```
# repro (short)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer test-token" -d '{"prompt":"long prompt...","max_tokens":512}'
# run 1000 concurrent requests with varying auth tokens
```
Result: high miss rate and tail latency ~200-400ms above baseline.
ben: Suspect root cause: key-normalization change from PR#489 (deployed 3 days ago) didn't strip intermittent suffixes (trailing slashes + case). We ended up with effectively duplicated prefix keys causing hotset fragmentation and eviction thrash.
marie: Confirmed timeline aligns with deploy. Immediate mitigations?
aj: Quick wins: 1) increase KV max_entries on the affected pool temporarily, 2) enable a conservative TTL for new keys (helps churn), 3) route heavy customers to dedicated pool if possible. I can bump max_entries on gpu-pool-east now.
taylor: Also pushed a canary that applies header normalization (lowercase + strip trailing) in the key builder on one canary node. Early numbers: miss rate down from 42% -> 6% on the canary.
ben: I'll prepare a targeted rollback/patch: revert the non-safe normalization changes from PR#489 and add deterministic normalization + unit tests. Then a migration job to coalesce duplicates by rehashing recent keys.
support-bot: Playbook step applied: added temporary rate-limit for non-essential internal jobs to reduce cache pressure.
marie: Customer impact: AcmeHealth reported p95 increased by ~250ms during spike. Support has offered credit; record that in the ticket. Please collect exact p95 deltas for billing adjustment.
aj: I ran the before/after query:
```
SELECT
  period,
  avg(p95) AS p95_ms,
  sum(kv_miss_count) AS misses
FROM metrics
WHERE pool = 'gpu-pool-east' AND time > now() - interval '2 hours'
GROUP BY period
ORDER BY period DESC
```
Before canary: misses 4200, p95 560ms. After canary: misses 580, p95 310ms (on canary slice).
taylor: Moving plan -> ben's patch to staging, run integration + load test, then canary with 5% traffic. If stable for 30m, ramp to 50% then 100%.
ben: PR ready (fix/key-normalize-489). I'll also add metrics to catch delta misses per prefix key and an alert when miss delta > 10% relative to baseline.
sre-oncall: I'll adjust alert thresholds and add a transient alert that triggers if miss-rate delta > 8% for 5m to catch regressions faster. I'll watch p99 and tail latency during rollout.
marie: Post-deploy followups: 1) postmortem owner = taylor, due EOD tomorrow; 2) schedule rehash job during low traffic window; 3) backfill unit/integration tests for key builder.
taylor: I'll add a small deterministic repro and include it in CI. Also adding a fuzz test that randomizes headers to ensure normalization invariants.
ben: Deploying staging now. ETA canary -> 21:30 UTC.
support-bot: Incident annotated: severity P2 -> resolved once rollout completes and metrics stable.
marie: Thanks team. Keep updates in-thread. Once stable I'll message acct team and close ticket. :thumbsup:
